schema:actionProcess.schema:name: Climate Profile
schema:actionProcess.schema:description: The Climate Profile Service is planned to provide a structured climatic baseline and future projections for the regions of the case studies.Existing analysis scripts (Python/R) will be adapted to operate as backend workflows.The service will ingest regional climate datasets (EURO-CORDEX) and observational references, compute standard climate indices, and store outputs in tabular format.

schema:step.schema:name: Raw Data Collection
schema:step.schema:description: Download historical and future climate projections from the Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) using the EU-CORDEX regional climate model. Data are retrieved for the selected area of interest and cropped to the study area before storage.

schema:step.schema:name: S1: Configure climate data request
schema:step.schema:description: Configure the climate model, emission scenario, temporal period, variables, and area of interest. The workflow iterates through the selected climate scenarios and variables.

schema:step.schema:name: S2: Download and crop climate datasets
schema:step.schema:description: For each selected scenario and climate variable, retrieve EU-CORDEX NetCDF files from CDS and crop them to the study area. Store the resulting datasets as NetCDF files. Output put in OUT_DIR

schema:step.schema:name: Climate Data Preparation
schema:step.schema:description: Combine cropped NetCDF files covering consecutive time periods into a single continuous climate dataset for the selected variable and scenario.

schema:step.schema:name: S3: Merge Cropped Climate Datasets
schema:step.schema:description: Identify all cropped NetCDF files corresponding to the selected climate variable and scenario, merge them into a single chronological dataset, remove duplicate timestamps, subset to the requested analysis period, and generate a final continuous NetCDF file.

schema:step.schema:name: Climate Indicator Generation
schema:step.schema:description: Transform daily climate datasets into annual climate indicators through unit conversion and temporal aggregation.

schema:step.schema:name: S4: Generate annual climate indicators
schema:step.schema:description: Convert climate variables to analysis units and aggregate daily observations into annual climate indicators. Temperature variables are converted from Kelvin to Celsius and averaged annually. Precipitation flux is converted to annual precipitation totals. The resulting datasets contain annual climate indicators for each grid point.

schema:step.schema:name: Climate Scenario Integration
schema:step.schema:description: Combine historical climate indicators with future climate scenario indicators to produce continuous climate projection datasets covering the full analysis horizon.

schema:step.schema:name: S5: Merge Historical and Scenario Climate Indicators
schema:step.schema:description: Merge annual climate indicator datasets from the historical period and future climate scenarios (RCP4.5 and RCP8.5), remove duplicate years, preserve metadata, and generate continuous climate projection datasets covering the full time horizon.

schema:result.schema:name: Climate Profile CSV
schema:result.schema:description: Climate profile time series exported as a comma-separated text file.

schema:result.schema:name: Climate Profile NetCDF
schema:result.schema:description: Climate profile time series exported as NetCDF.

schema:step.schema:name: S6.1: Extract Climate Indicator Time Series
schema:step.schema:description: Read annual climate indicator datasets for the selected scenario and identify climate variables available for analysis.

schema:step.schema:name: S6.2: Compute Spatial Mean Time Series
schema:step.schema:description: Calculate annual spatial averages for each climate indicator by averaging across all spatial dimensions while preserving the annual dimension.

schema:step.schema:name: S6.3: Export Climate Profile Outputs
schema:step.schema:description:
Combine spacial average for annual scenario for each variable 
1.	Annual timeseries of RR (total): Sum of daily precipitation values for each year
2.	Annual timeseries of TX (average): Average of daily values for each year
3.	Annual timeseries of TG (average): Average of daily values for each year
4.	Annual timeseries of TM (average): Average of daily values for each year
5.	Annual timeseries of WS (average): Average of daily values for each year
6.	Annual timeseries of RH (average): Average of daily values for each year

Converting into a table with a variable per column

schema:step.schema:name: Compute temperature indices
schema:step.schema:description: Compute temperature indices: Summer Days (SU), Hot Days (HD), Tropical Nights (TR).
